st.1: The First Amendment (1951) inserted in Article 19(2) the power to prescribe professional or technical qualifications and to create State monopolies.
st.3: 'Public order' was added to Article 19(2) by the Sixteenth Amendment.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because those powers were inserted in Article 19(6), not 19(2), and 3 is wrong because 'public order' was added by the First Amendment (1951).

st.3: Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended under Article 359.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because since the 44th Amendment Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359.
Both statements are correct: V.G. Row (1952) laid down the test of reasonableness, and courts decide reasonableness so that a restriction does not eclipse the right.

st.1: The First Backward Classes Commission, set up in January 1953, was headed by B.P. Mandal.
st.2: The B.P. Mandal Commission was set up by the V.P. Singh Government.

x: Statement 3 only is correct; 1 is wrong because the First Commission was headed by Kaka Kalelkar, and 2 is wrong because the Mandal Commission was set up by the Janata Government of Morarji Desai – V.P. Singh only implemented it.

st.2: Article 350A deals with mother-tongue instruction at the secondary stage.
st.3: Article 350B deals with the development of Hindi.
st.4: Article 351 deals with a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because Article 350A concerns the primary stage, 3 is wrong because Article 350B provides the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, and 4 is wrong because Article 351 deals with the development of Hindi.

st.2: It is a duty of the State to provide education to children aged 6 to 14 years.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because Article 51A(k) is a duty of parents or guardians, not the State – the State's duty is in Article 21A.

st.2: The 42nd Amendment moved forests and protection of wild animals and birds to the State List.
st.4: Part IVA is one of four Parts added after 1950, all of them by the 42nd Amendment.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the 42nd Amendment moved these subjects to the Concurrent List, and 4 is wrong because only Parts IVA and XIVA came by the 42nd Amendment (IXA by the 74th, IXB by the 97th).

st.3: Golaknath (1967) was decided by an 11-judge bench and arose from a challenge to the 24th Amendment.
st.4: Kesavananda Bharati was the first case to hold that Parliament cannot amend (abridge) Fundamental Rights.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because Golaknath arose from a challenge to the 17th Amendment – the 24th Amendment came later in response to it – and 4 is wrong because Golaknath, not Kesavananda, first held that Parliament cannot abridge Fundamental Rights.

st.2: Fundamental Rights can be waived by the person concerned.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because Fundamental Rights cannot be waived (doctrine of non-waiver).

st.3: Under Article 240, the President makes regulations for the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because Article 240 regulations cover UTs such as Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep, not Delhi, which has its own legislature.

st.1: The post is mentioned in Article 75 of the Constitution.
st.3: He enjoys the powers of the Prime Minister.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because the post of Deputy Prime Minister is not mentioned in the Constitution, and 3 is wrong because he has no special powers beyond those of a Minister.

st.2: When he addresses the Houses, the President sits in Parliament as a member.
st.3: Articles 79 to 122, dealing with Parliament, are in Part VI of the Constitution.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because the President is an integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House, and 3 is wrong because Articles 79 to 122 are in Part V.

st.2: Of the 24 DRSCs since 2004, 16 function under the Rajya Sabha and 8 under the Lok Sabha.
st.4: Ministers are eligible to be members of a DRSC.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is reversed – 16 DRSCs are under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha – and 4 is wrong because Ministers cannot be members of a DRSC.

st.2: Once such a resolution is passed, Parliament is bound to enact the law.
st.3: The resolution is sent to Parliament only after it is recommended by the Governor.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because Parliament is not bound to act on the resolution, and 3 is wrong because no Governor's recommendation is needed.

st.1: A no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers can be moved in either House of Parliament.
st.3: The oath of secrecy that keeps Cabinet deliberations confidential is administered to Union Ministers by the Vice-President.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because a no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha, and 3 is wrong because Union Ministers take the oath of secrecy before the President.

st.2: He must be qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the Advocate General must be qualified to be a High Court judge, not a Supreme Court judge.

st.3: The National Commission hears complaints above ₹2 crore, and appeals from it lie to the High Court.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; 3 is wrong because appeals from the National Commission lie to the Supreme Court, not the High Court.

st.1: Like Britain's C&AG, he controls the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund, so he is a Comptroller as well as an Auditor General.
st.2: He can disallow irregular expenditure and enforce recovery of the amount.

x: Statement 3 only is correct; 1 is wrong because, unlike Britain's C&AG, he has no control over the issue of money and is only an Auditor General, and 2 is wrong because he cannot disallow expenditure or enforce recovery.

st.2: Personal patronage is a feature of Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because Weber's bureaucracy is impersonal and merit-based – patronage is one of Morstein Marx's other types.

st.2: The Chief Election Commissioner is removed in the same manner as a High Court judge.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the CEC is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge.

st.2: The 2019 amendment cut the SHRC's strength from five to three.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct; 2 is wrong because the SHRC was cut from five to three (Chairperson + two members) in 2006, not 2019.

st.2: Complaints registered in 2025-26 (up to February 2026) were fewer than in 2024-25.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is reversed – 389 complaints were registered in 2025-26 (to February 2026), more than the 292 of 2024-25.

st.2: India's CPI 2025 score was lower than its 2024 score.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is reversed – India's score rose from 38 (2024) to 39 (2025).
All three statements are correct: the 2018 Amendment made bribe-giving a direct offence (up to 7 years), made commercial organisations liable, and aligned the law with UNCAC.

st.3: Optional schemes are funded 50:50 for all States without exception.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; 3 is wrong because optional schemes are 50:50 generally but 80:20 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

st.3: The Centre alone can pass a decision of the Council.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because the Centre has only one-third of the votes and a decision needs a three-fourths majority, so it cannot pass a decision alone.

st.2: An RUPP need not report donations above Rs 20,000 to the Election Commission.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because an RUPP must report donations above Rs 20,000 to the Election Commission.

st.2: The VVPAT was first used in the 2014 Lok Sabha general election.
st.3: The EVMs currently used by the ECI can record up to 2,000 votes and need an external power supply.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because the VVPAT was first used in the Noksen (Nagaland) bye-election of 2013, and 3 is wrong because EVMs run on a battery power pack and need no external power supply.

st.3: Disputes relating to the election of the President are decided by Parliament.
st.4: From 1 July 2024, electoral offences such as bribery and personation are in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because Presidential election disputes are decided by the Supreme Court, and 4 is wrong because electoral offences are in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), not the BNSS.

st.2: Under Section 81, an election petition must be filed in the Supreme Court within 45 days.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because an election petition is filed in the High Court, not the Supreme Court.

st.3: The intermediate tier must be omitted in States with a population below 20 lakh.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because in States with a population below 20 lakh the intermediate tier may be omitted – it is optional, not compulsory.

st.3: It extends Part IX to both the Fifth Schedule Areas and the Sixth Schedule Tribal Areas.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because PESA extends Part IX only to the Fifth Schedule Areas.

st.1: It is a Centrally sponsored scheme launched on 20 April 2021.
st.3: The benefit applies only to loans exceeding ₹1 lakh.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because YSR Zero Interest Crop Loans is an Andhra Pradesh State scheme, and 3 is wrong because the benefit applies to crop loans up to ₹1 lakh repaid on time.

st.1: Its coastline, remeasured at 1,053.07 km, is the second longest in India after Gujarat.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct; 1 is wrong because on remeasurement Andhra Pradesh's coastline is the third longest, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

st.2: Community Forest Management began in 2002.
st.4: Andhra Pradesh was sanctioned 61 Nagar Vans under the Nagar Van Yojana of the Ministry of Rural Development.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; 4 is wrong because the Nagar Van Yojana belongs to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, not Rural Development.

st.3: Years of schooling is one of its seven standard-of-living indicators.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because years of schooling is an education indicator, not a standard-of-living one.

st.2: According to the Economic Survey 2018-19, the dividend will peak around 2041.
st.4: The 60+ share is expected to fall to about 16% by 2041.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; 4 is wrong because the 60+ share will rise, not fall – from 8.6% in 2011 to about 16% by 2041.

st.4: The urban heat island effect is most pronounced around midday.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; 4 is wrong because the urban heat island is most pronounced at night, when the city releases stored heat.

st.2: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging IRDP and TRYSEM.
st.3: The Family Planning Programme was part of the strategy of 'direct attack on poverty'.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because the JRY merged NREP and RLEGP, and 3 is wrong because Family Planning is a population measure, not part of the direct attack on poverty.

st.2: The Madanapalle Water Grid is meant mainly for drought-prone north coastal Andhra.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct; 2 is wrong because the Madanapalle Water Grid serves drought-prone Rayalaseema, not north coastal Andhra.

st.1: Realised investment always equals planned investment.
st.3: If planned saving exceeds planned investment, output and income rise.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because realised investment equals planned plus unplanned investment, and 3 is reversed – when planned saving exceeds planned investment, output and income fall.
Both statements are correct: services is the largest sectoral source of India's national income and the household sector the largest institutional source.

st.1: GSDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + production taxes − production subsidies.
st.3: The GSDP of Andhra Pradesh is compiled by the NSO using the production approach.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because GSDP at market prices adds product taxes and subtracts product subsidies (production taxes and subsidies take factor cost to basic prices), and 3 is wrong because AP's GSDP is compiled by the State Directorate of Economics and Statistics, not the NSO.
Both statements are correct: a sector growing slower than GDP loses share in GDP, though its absolute output may still rise.

st.1: The Second UN Decade for the Eradication of Poverty (2008-2017) was proclaimed by the World Bank.
st.3: SDG 1 aims to end hunger, achieve food security and improve nutrition by 2030.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because the UN Decades were proclaimed by the UN General Assembly, not the World Bank, and 3 is wrong because SDG 1 aims to end poverty in all its forms – ending hunger is SDG 2.

st.1: It is a statutory body set up by an Act of Parliament in 1952.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; 1 is wrong because the NDC was neither constitutional nor statutory – it was set up by an executive resolution in 1952.

st.1: The State Planning Commission of Andhra Pradesh was set up only after district-level decentralised planning had begun.
st.3: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region covers 10 districts and is assisted by the World Bank.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct; 1 is wrong because the State Planning Commission came in the Fifth Plan, before district planning began in the Sixth Plan, and 3 is wrong because the Visakhapatnam Economic Region is NITI Aayog-assisted, not World Bank-assisted.

st.2: Under Article 269, taxes on inter-State sale and consignment of goods levied and collected by the Union are kept wholly by the Union.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because Article 269 taxes, though levied and collected by the Union, are assigned to the States.

st.2: The 16th FC marks a shift from performance-based to entitlement-based transfers.
st.3: Critics argue that fiscal capacity is uniform across States, so devolution equalises States by itself.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is reversed – the 16th FC marks a shift from entitlement to performance – and 3 is wrong because critics say fiscal capacity is not uniform, so devolution alone does not equalise States.

st.2: The Governing Council was first constituted in February 2015 under an Act of Parliament and took over the work of the NDC.
st.3: Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are convened by the President.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because NITI Aayog and its Governing Council rest on an executive (Cabinet) resolution, not an Act of Parliament, and 3 is wrong because Regional Councils are convened by the Prime Minister.

st.2: NITI Aayog prepares the Five Year Plans.
st.3: The Union Finance Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because NITI Aayog does not prepare Five Year Plans, and 3 is wrong because the Prime Minister is its ex-officio Chairperson.

st.3: YSR Kadapa was dropped after the 2022 reorganisation.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because YSR Kadapa continues in the programme – only the parent districts of Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam were replaced.

st.2: Coins are minted by the RBI and only distributed by the Government of India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is reversed – coins are minted by the Government of India and only distributed by the RBI.

st.2: Rohit Jain was appointed a Deputy Governor in May 2026 by the RBI Central Board, replacing T. Rabi Sankar.
st.3: The RBI's four Local Boards are at Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and Hyderabad.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because Deputy Governors are appointed by the Central Government, not the RBI Board, and 3 is wrong because the fourth Local Board is at New Delhi, not Hyderabad.

st.1: The new CPI-Combined series released on 12 February 2026 has 2024 as its base year and is compiled by the RBI.
st.2: Failure to meet the target is deemed when average CPI inflation stays above 6% or below 2% for three consecutive months.

x: Statement 3 only is correct; 1 is wrong because CPI-C is compiled by the NSO (MoSPI), not the RBI, and 2 is wrong because failure is deemed after three consecutive quarters, not months.

st.1: Financial assets exceeding 50% of total assets is by itself enough to qualify.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because both conditions – financial assets above 50% of total assets and financial income above 50% of gross income – must be met.

st.2: Bank loans to micro and small enterprises must be collateral-free up to ₹20 lakh, but PMEGP units are excluded.
st.3: The DRI scheme was introduced by NABARD in April 1972.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because all PMEGP units are also covered by collateral-free lending, and 3 is wrong because NABARD was set up only in 1982 – the DRI scheme was a Government/RBI scheme.

st.2: The 14 banks nationalised in 1969 had deposits of ₹50 crore and above, and the State Bank of India was among them.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the State Bank of India was nationalised separately in 1955, not among the 14 banks of 1969.

st.2: The 2008 global crisis and weak exports eased the stress on bank loans.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is reversed – the 2008 crisis and weak exports added to the stress.

st.1: Under Section 13(2), lenders holding 75% of the dues (60% before the 2016 amendment) may issue a 60-day notice.
st.3: Under Section 17, an appeal lies to the DRAT within 45 days.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is reversed – the threshold was cut from 75% to 60% by the 2016 amendment – and 3 is wrong because a Section 17 appeal lies to the DRT, not the DRAT.

st.1: A vote on account is provided for under Article 115 of the Constitution.
st.2: A vote on account is passed only after a full discussion of the demands for grants.

x: Statement 3 only is correct; 1 is wrong because the vote on account is under Article 116, and 2 is wrong because a vote on account is normally passed without discussion.

st.1: The plan/non-plan distinction was removed in 2017-18 on the recommendation of the Fourteenth Finance Commission.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; 1 is wrong because the plan/non-plan merger followed the Rangarajan Committee's recommendation, not the Fourteenth Finance Commission's.

st.2: NAMA-11 is a WTO coalition on agricultural subsidies.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because NAMA-11 deals with non-agricultural (industrial) market access, not agriculture.

st.3: India is one of its founding members.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; 3 is wrong because India walked out of the RCEP negotiations in 2019 and is not a member.

st.3: India is the largest producer but only the second largest consumer of pulses.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because India is both the largest producer and the largest consumer of pulses.

st.4: Central assistance is given as an interest-free loan for the full drone cost.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; 4 is wrong because central assistance is a grant of 80% of the drone cost, up to Rs 8 lakh, not a loan.

st.3: The genome-edited rice DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from MTU 1010.
st.4: SDN-3 genome-edited varieties carry no foreign DNA and therefore fall outside the GMO rules.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from Samba Mahsuri (BPT 5204), and 4 is wrong because it is SDN-1 (and SDN-2) editing that carries no foreign DNA – SDN-3 involves foreign DNA.

st.2: Coarse grains are procured exclusively by the FCI.
st.3: Decentralised Procurement was introduced in 1997, under which the FCI alone procures and stores the grain.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because coarse grains are procured mainly by State agencies, and 3 is wrong because under Decentralised Procurement the States themselves procure, store and distribute the grain.

st.1: As of April 2026, there were 14 Navratna and 27 Maharatna CPSEs.
st.2: NALCO, a Navratna headquartered at Bhubaneswar, functions under the Ministry of Steel.

x: Statement 3 only is correct; 1 is reversed – there were 14 Maharatna and 27 Navratna CPSEs – and 2 is wrong because NALCO functions under the Ministry of Mines.

st.1: The Chittoor NIMZ received final approval in 2016.
st.3: In-principle approval was given for NIMZs at Chittoor and Prakasam in August 2013 under the SEZ Act, 2005.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because it was the Prakasam NIMZ that got final approval in 2016, and 3 is wrong because NIMZs come under the National Manufacturing Policy 2011, not the SEZ Act.

st.2: It functioned under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because the BIFR functioned under the Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services).

st.1: The 14th Finance Commission gave a single award for undivided Andhra Pradesh.
st.4: The 16th Finance Commission ended revenue-deficit grants for all States, and AP's divisible-pool share fell to 4.22%.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; 1 is wrong because the 14th FC gave separate awards for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and 4 is wrong because AP's share rose, not fell, to 4.22%.

st.1: The Gender Budget is Statement 13, presented since 2005-06, and covers only schemes meant 100% for women.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because the Gender Budget covers both 100% women-specific schemes (Part A) and schemes with 30-99% allocation for women (Part B).

st.1: Guarantees are direct liabilities that must be serviced every year whether or not they are invoked.
st.2: Guarantees are included in AP's outstanding debt.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct; 1 is wrong because guarantees are contingent liabilities that fall due only when invoked, and 2 is wrong because guarantees are not included in outstanding debt.

st.2: Secunderabad is one of the divisions of South Coast Railway.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct; 2 is wrong because Secunderabad is the headquarters of South Central Railway, not a South Coast Railway division.

st.1: Tax incentives notified in 2015 under Section 94(1) apply only to the backward districts of Andhra Pradesh.
st.3: For Polavaram, the Centre bears the full cost at current price levels.

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because Section 94(1) tax incentives cover both successor States, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and 3 is wrong because the Centre limits its Polavaram liability to old price levels.

st.1: It is also called 'Kalinga Andhra' and its 6 districts include Kakinada.
st.3: ASR district ranked first in the Aspirational Districts Programme theme of Health and Nutrition (March 2026).

x: Statement 2 only is correct; 1 is wrong because Kakinada is in the Godavari region – the six Uttarandhra districts run from Srikakulam to ASR – and 3 is wrong because ASR ranked first in Basic Infrastructure, not Health and Nutrition.

st.3: The Union Cabinet approved it on 15 March 2016.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; 3 is wrong because the package was announced in September 2016 and approved by the Union Cabinet on 15 March 2017.

st.1: The AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project covers 565 minor-tank villages and is funded by the Asian Development Bank.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct; 1 is wrong because APIIATP is a World Bank project, not an ADB project.

st.2: The Agriculture and Allied Budget 2026-27 (about Rs 53,753 crore) was presented by Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav.
st.3: The 2026-27 budget gives the Price Stabilisation Fund a larger allocation than irrigation.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct; 2 is wrong because the agriculture budget was presented by Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu (for the third time), and 3 is wrong because the Price Stabilisation Fund gets Rs 500 crore against Rs 14,277 crore for irrigation.

st.1: The National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) is headquartered at Kochi.
st.2: Training and capacity building under PMMSY is handled by MPEDA, not by the NFDB.

x: Statement 3 only is correct; 1 is wrong because the NFDB is headquartered at Hyderabad (Kochi is MPEDA's base), and 2 is reversed – PMMSY training is handled by the NFDB, not MPEDA.

st.2: The National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres at Chintaladevi (Nellore) and Itarsi were set up under the National Livestock Mission.
st.3: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Livestock requires collateral security for dairy and poultry loans.

x: Statement 1 only is correct; 2 is wrong because the National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres come under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, and 3 is wrong because the scheme backs collateral-free loans.

st.3: Its core hubs include a Finance Hub along with People and Land Hubs.
st.4: Its stated goal is faceless, paperless and cashless governance, beginning with computerised land registration.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because e-Pragati's core hubs are People, Land, Entity, GIS and IoT – there is no Finance Hub – and 4 is wrong because computerised land registration was CARD (1998), not an e-Pragati aim.

st.1: It was issued by the Industries and Commerce Department.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; 1 is wrong because the policy was issued by the ITE&C (Information Technology, Electronics and Communications) Department.
Both statements are correct: the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub targets 20,000 start-ups and 1 lakh jobs in five years under the AP Innovation and Startup Policy 2024-29.

st.2: The Fund of Funds for Startups, managed by SIDBI, invests directly in start-ups.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the Fund of Funds does not invest directly – it invests through SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds.

st.3: It is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because SVAMITVA is a scheme of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, not Rural Development.

st.2: Profit maximisation and growth at any cost are among its objectives.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because sustainable development rejects growth at any cost – it balances growth with inclusion and the environment.

st.2: The Sustainable Development Goals comprise 17 goals and 169 targets and are legally binding on member states.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the SDGs are not legally binding – they are a voluntary global agenda.

st.2: India does not follow Daylight Saving Time.

x: Both statements are correct: under Daylight Saving Time clocks are advanced by one hour in summer, and India does not follow it.

st.3: Of the eight States it crosses, Gujarat is the first and Mizoram the last from west to east.

x: All three statements are correct: the Tropic of Cancer lies at about 23°26'N, divides India into almost equal halves, and crosses eight States from Gujarat to Mizoram.

st.3: The magnetic axis coincides exactly with the geographic axis.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; 3 is wrong because the magnetic axis is inclined at about 11° to the geographic axis – it does not coincide with it.

st.4: Clay is porous but impermeable.

x: All four statements are correct: sedimentary rocks cover about 75% of the surface, rock salt and gypsum are chemically formed, sandstone, shale and conglomerate are clastic, and clay is porous but impermeable.

st.2: Intensity increases with distance from the epicentre.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct; 2 is reversed – intensity decreases with distance from the epicentre.

st.4: The Appalachians are a product of the Tertiary orogeny.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; 4 is wrong because the Appalachians are old fold mountains of the Palaeozoic (Caledonian–Hercynian) orogenies, not the Tertiary.

st.3: A sill is a near-vertical wall cutting across rock layers.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because a sill is a horizontal sheet lying along the layers – a near-vertical wall is a dyke.

st.1: India's continental shelf is broadest off Tamil Nadu.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; 1 is wrong because India's continental shelf is broadest off the west coast, off Gujarat (Gulf of Khambhat), not Tamil Nadu.

st.2: The Salween flows south to the Andaman Sea.

x: All three statements are correct: the Amur flows to the Sea of Okhotsk, the Salween flows south to the Andaman Sea, and the Tigris and Euphrates form the Shatt al-Arab.

st.1: It is a cold low-pressure region around the poles that rotates clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; 1 is wrong because the polar vortex rotates anticlockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.

st.3: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, its coastline of about 1,053 km is longer than Tamil Nadu's.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 3 is wrong because Tamil Nadu's coastline (about 1,068 km) is longer – Andhra Pradesh is third, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

st.2: Water vapour in the air increases with latitude.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is reversed – water vapour decreases with latitude (from the equator to the poles).

st.1: The Malwa Plateau has two drainage systems, one towards the Arabian Sea and one towards the Bay of Bengal.

x: All three statements are correct: the Malwa Plateau drains both to the Arabian Sea and to the Bay of Bengal, the Vindhyas lie to its south, and the Bhander Plateau forms the southern Vindhyan scarpland.

st.2: Ocean Mean Temperature (OMT) is the average temperature of the upper ocean down to the 26 °C isotherm.

x: All three statements are correct: the LPA (1971–2020) is 868.6 mm, OMT is measured down to the 26 °C isotherm, and OMT predicts monsoon rainfall better than SST.

st.2: The Brahmaputra is called the 'sorrow of Bihar'.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the Kosi, not the Brahmaputra, is called the 'sorrow of Bihar'.

All three statements are correct: the Ongole–Machilipatnam stretch is the most cyclone-vulnerable, Nellore and Srikakulam are the most exposed districts, and Cyclone Laila (2010) crossed near Bapatla.

st.2: The river with the longest course inside Andhra Pradesh is the Krishna.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; 2 is wrong because the longest course inside Andhra Pradesh is that of the Penna (536 km), not the Krishna.

st.2: Its black colour comes mainly from humus.
